en.name: Plantain flour
en.summary: Plantain flour is unripe plantain dried and milled, used for amala and as a thickener. Sealed in a cool dark cupboard it keeps about 6–12 months — a figure borrowed from white flour, since no source publishes one for plantain flour. It is stable while dry and finished once it is not.
en.pantry: A sealed jar in a cool, dark cupboard, away from the stove, gives about 6–12 months. Like other dried starch flours it is stable while dry and finished once it is not: clumping, a musty smell, or any visible mould means the bag drew moisture, and a dried food that has reabsorbed water is not saved by drying it out again. Check stored bags every so often rather than assuming. It darkens with age, which is the fruit's own phenolics oxidising — a quality change rather than a safety one, though a very dark flour will make a darker amala.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for plantain flour, so none is given. In a very humid climate a genuinely airtight container in the fridge is a reasonable precaution against damp, but the seal has to be real and the container must come back to room temperature before opening, or you will condense water straight into the flour — the exact failure you were trying to avoid. Made-up amala is a cooked starch and belongs in the fridge promptly, not on the counter.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for plantain flour either. Freezing a sealed bag deals with pantry insects in a bulk purchase and slows the darkening a little, but neither makes it a documented shelf life, and this page will not invent one. Buying smaller bags more often is the better answer in a humid kitchen.
spoilage: Clumps that will not break up — the flour has taken up water.
A musty or mouldy smell, as opposed to the flour's normal faintly green, starchy one.
Any visible mould, including specks in the seams of the bag.
Weevils, small moths, webbing or fine dust in the packet.
tips: Decant into an airtight jar as soon as you get it home.
Store away from the sink and the kettle; steam is the real threat.
Expect it to darken with age — that is oxidation, not spoilage.
Refrigerate made-up amala promptly and reheat it thoroughly.

faq.q: How long does plantain flour keep?
faq.a: About 6–12 months in a sealed jar in a cool, dark cupboard. The figure is read across from white flour.

faq.q: Why has my plantain flour gone darker?
faq.a: The fruit's own phenolic compounds oxidise over time. It is a quality change, not a sign that the flour is unsafe.
Yes, if it takes up moisture. Clumping, a musty smell or visible mould all mean the bag got damp, and it should be thrown out.

zh.name: 大蕉粉
zh.summary: 大蕉粉是把未熟的大蕉乾燥後研磨而成，用來做 amala，也可以當增稠劑。密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 6～12 個月——這個數字借自白麵粉，因為沒有任何來源替大蕉粉公布過期限。它在乾燥時很穩定，一旦不乾燥就結束了。
zh.pantry: 密封裝罐、放陰涼避光、遠離爐火的櫥櫃，約 6～12 個月。和其他乾燥澱粉粉類一樣，它乾燥時穩定、受潮就完蛋：結塊、有霉味，或看得見任何霉，都代表袋子吸了水，而重新吸水的乾燥食品不是再烘乾一次就能救回來的。存放的袋子要不時檢查，不要放著就當它沒事。它會隨時間變深色，那是果實本身的多酚類氧化——屬於品質變化而非安全問題，不過顏色很深的粉做出來的 amala 也會比較深。
zh.fridge: 大蕉粉沒有公布的冷藏期限，所以本頁不給。在非常潮濕的氣候，用真正密封的容器放冰箱是合理的防潮措施，但密封必須確實，容器也要先回到室溫再開，否則你會把水直接凝進粉裡——正是你想避免的那種失敗。調好的 amala 是熟澱粉，要盡快冷藏，不能放在檯面上。
zh.freezer: 大蕉粉也沒有給冷凍數字。把密封袋冷凍可以解決大量採購的櫥櫃害蟲，也稍微延緩變色，但這都不足以構成有出處的保存期限，本頁不會憑空生一個。在潮濕的廚房裡，更好的答案是少量多次地買。
spoilage: 結成撥不開的塊——粉已經吸水。
聞到霉味（正常應該是淡淡的青味與澱粉味）。
看得見任何霉，包括袋子縫隙裡的小斑點。
袋內有米象、小蛾、絲網或細粉屑。
tips: 遠離水槽和熱水瓶；蒸氣才是真正的威脅。
顏色隨時間變深是正常的氧化，不是壞掉。
調好的 amala 要盡快冷藏，復熱要徹底。

faq.a: 密封裝罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 6～12 個月。這個數字是從白麵粉讀過來的。

faq.q: 大蕉粉為什麼變深色了？
faq.a: 果實本身的多酚類隨時間氧化。這是品質變化，不代表不能吃。
會，只要它吸了水。結塊、霉味或看得見的霉都代表受潮，應該整包丟掉。
